title: Stewart Organization, Inc. v. Ricoh Corp. (1988)
summary: The federal transfer statute governed the treatment of the forum-selection clause in deciding whether to transfer the diversity action.
notes: Atlantic Marine later clarifies the weight of a valid clause under § 1404. Preserve the chronology: Stewart’s historical factor discussion and Atlantic Marine’s later framework are connected, not interchangeable.

sections.Parties: Stewart, an Alabama dealer, sued Ricoh over their commercial relationship.
sections.Material Facts: The parties’ agreement selected a Manhattan forum. Stewart nevertheless sued in Alabama, whose policy was hostile to forum-selection clauses. Ricoh sought transfer under § 1404(a), creating a question about the relationship between that federal statute and the state’s policy.
sections.Procedural History: The Supreme Court required use of the federal statutory transfer analysis. It did not simply treat the state’s policy as dispositive.
sections.Issue: Did state policy against the clause determine the federal court’s transfer decision, or did § 1404 govern?
sections.Holding: Section 1404 governed. The clause was an important factor in the federal statutory inquiry, alongside the other relevant considerations.
sections.Reasoning: The Court identified an enacted federal statute that addressed transfer for convenience and the interests of justice. The state policy could not replace the multifactor judgment Congress assigned to the federal court. This placed the case on a different analytic footing from an unguided federal common-law choice under Erie. The Court’s treatment left a role for the circumstances of the litigation rather than making the state policy or the clause alone mechanically controlling.

learning.why: The federal transfer statute governed the treatment of the forum-selection clause in deciding whether to transfer the diversity action.

topics.cp-rule-scope: Section 1404 supplied federal transfer authority even though state law disfavored the contractual forum provision.
topics.forum-selection: The contractual choice was a significant consideration within the transfer analysis.
topics.cp-transfer: The forum clause affected a discretionary federal transfer decision.
topics.cp-judicial-discretion: Stewart requires the federal transfer decision to consider the forum-selection clause within the statutory convenience-and-justice inquiry.

learning.separateOpinions: Justice Kennedy favored giving very substantial weight to the contractual choice. Justice Scalia dissented, disputing the claimed conflict and the displacement of state treatment of the agreement.

mnemonic.rationale: A forum clause weighed under section 1404
